text:
amy_support: FYI - customer reported a burst where they got a mix of 429s and a few 401s during peak traffic. They say it only started after an aggressive retry burst from their side. attaching quick repro + logs below.

oliver_prod_ops: which customer / region? any request ids?

amy_support: tenant acct-987, primary region us-west-2. sample curl + response from their logs: ```
$ curl -i -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-region-served: us-west-2
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-request-id: abc123
Retry-After: 3
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}
```
They also pasted a couple responses that were 401s with `invalid_token` and those trace IDs were served from eu-west-1.

jasmine_sre: interesting — 401s only when route flips to eu-west-1? could be auth-key cache miss or stale KMS/validator sync. can you paste the trace map (request id -> region)?

amy_support: pasted mapping: abc123 -> us-west-2 (429), def456 -> eu-west-1 (401), ghi789 -> eu-west-1 (401), jkl012 -> us-west-2 (200). The routing log shows: us-west-2 hit capacity threshold and then we applied cross-region fallback to eu-west-1.

oliver_prod_ops: that matches our routing policy: fallback allowed for that tenant, but we should not be returning 401s from fallback. 401 implies auth verification failed in eu-west-1. could be replication lag for API key signer or a missing secret in that region.

rachel_oncall: billing-bot just flagged a token spike for acct-987 (spike at T+2m). retry loop causing double-counting is likely. @jasmine_sre can you check auth-validate service in eu-west-1 for time drift / missing keys? :eyes:

jasmine_sre: checking now. quick grep shows our auth-keys table had a 2m replication lag to eu-west-1 during that window. key_id 99f4 was inserted in primary but not yet visible in eu-west-1 when fallback started. that explains the 401s.

amy_support: nice find. so the flow is: us-west saturated -> fallback to eu -> eu doesn't yet see key -> returns 401 -> client retries -> we see more traffic -> more cross-region fallbacks -> 429s and billing spike.

oliver_prod_ops: this is a tough interaction: fallback solves availability but must guarantee auth metadata present. mitigation options: (1) prefer queueing in-origin until short backlog drains, (2) make fallback wait until auth metadata sync confirmed, or (3) attempt token introspection to primary region before sending to fallback.

jasmine_sre: short-term we can flip a per-tenant override to disable cross-region fallback (let them queue or get 429s from origin) until key sync is healthy. I've verified the replication window is small but it happened during a config deploy that slowed replication.

deploy-bot: config update for routing-override applied for tenant acct-987 by rachel_oncall at 1713010500. change id cfg-2024-xy.

billing-bot: billing alert: detected 2.1M token spike in us-west-2 for acct-987 between 1713009800-1713010200. Suspicious retry-loop pattern. No automatic billing pause applied.

rachel_oncall: applied temporary routing override to block cross-region handoff for tenant, and raised replication alert to dev-infra. monitoring panels: 429 rate dropped ~70% in the following 5m.

amy_support: verified with customer — they stopped seeing 401s/429s after our temporary change. customer reduced client retries too. they want a postmortem and a durable fix for fallback auth guarantee.

ojline: (typo, ignore)

jasmine_sre: next steps I've noted: 1) add guard so fallback only happens if auth metadata present (fast check), 2) surface per-tenant replication status in Console (so support can flip override preemptively), 3) consider conservative default where fallback prefers capacity-based queue on origin for short windows.

oliver_prod_ops: agree. also add a metric that correlates cross-region failovers with 401s. that'll help alert earlier.

rachel_oncall: opening an internal incident ticket INC-2024-089 to track fixes and customer postmortem. assigning to jasmine_sre (auth/replication owner) and oliver_prod_ops (routing owner).

amy_support: I'll draft a short customer-facing summary and share the timeline + mitigation.

jasmine_sre: quick note — deploy that adds an extra replication throttle was the proximate cause. I've flagged it to infra. we'll try to get a patch that ensures new keys are promoted to all fallback regions before allowing fallback.

oliver_prod_ops: thanks team. can we add a short-lived mitigation in runtime: if fallback region returns 401 for the same key within X seconds, treat it as auth-replication-miss and avoid counting as a billable attempt until revalidated? (we'll need accounting input).

rachel_oncall: good idea. billing-bot, please help define a non-billable retry window for auth-replication misses — tagging finance/special-cases.

billing-bot: acknowledged. creating ticket BILL-578 with suggested non-billable window of 30s for auth-replication-miss cases.

amy_support: closing loop with customer in 1h after we finalize the PM. thanks all :thumbsup:
